title: Where Does the Performance Go? Understanding and Recovering Performance Regressions in C-to-Rust Translation
title_zh: C到Rust翻译中性能去了哪？理解并恢复C到Rust翻译中的性能回退

paragraphs.en: Rust is increasingly adopted as a memory-safe successor to C, and transpilers such as c2rust can migrate entire C projects while preserving their behavior. Preserving behavior, however, does not guarantee preserving performance. We study this gap on 20 real-world C projects and their c2rust translations. On the eight projects used for analysis, the translated Rust is more than 3% slower than the original C on 12 of 19 operations, by up to 62.2%. By comparing execution-cost profiles, optimized LLVM IR, and compiler optimization remarks across each C–Rust pair, we trace these slowdowns to nine recurring performance issues, spanning residual runtime work, missed compiler optimizations, and C-style source patterns, and derive an optimization direction for each. We then present PerfR , an LLM-based approach that encodes these issues as reusable optimization rules to recover the performance of translated Rust. PerfR profiles each project to locate hot functions and matches them against rule-specific patterns. The LLM then checks each rule’s rewrite preconditions against the project context before rewriting, and a rewrite is kept only if it passes both functional and performance validation. On 41 operations from twelve held-out projects, PerfR preserves C outputs on all tested workloads and speeds up 40 operations over the c2rust translations, 18 of which end up faster than the original C. It outperforms the general-purpose coding agent Codex on 31 of the 37 operations where both preserve C outputs, and outperforms its own variant without rule guidance on 34 of the 41 operations.
paragraphs.zh: Rust 正日益被采用为 C 的内存安全后继语言，而 c2rust 等转译器能够在保留行为的前提下迁移整个 C 项目。 然而，保留行为并不保证保留性能。 我们在 20 个真实世界的 C 项目及其 c2rust 翻译版本上研究了这一差距。 在用于分析的八个项目中，翻译后的 Rust 在 19 个操作中的 12 个上比原始 C 慢超过 3%，最多慢 62.2%。 通过比较每个 C–Rust 配对的执行开销剖析、优化后的 LLVM IR 以及编译器优化备注，我们将这些减速追溯到九个反复出现的性能问题，涵盖残留的运行时工作、错失的编译器优化以及 C 风格的源代码模式，并为每个问题推导出优化方向。 随后我们提出 PerfR，这是一种基于大语言模型的方法，它将这些问题编码为可复用的优化规则，以恢复翻译后的 Rust 的性能。 PerfR 对每个项目进行剖析以定位热点函数，并将其与规则特定的模式进行匹配。 大语言模型随后在重写之前根据项目上下文检查每条规则的重写前提条件，且只有当重写同时通过功能验证和性能验证时才会被保留。 在来自十二个保留项目的 41 个操作上，PerfR 在所有测试工作负载上都保持了与 C 相同的输出，并使 40 个操作相对于 c2rust 翻译版本得到加速，其中 18 个最终比原始 C 更快。 在两者都保持 C 输出的 37 个操作中的 31 个上，它优于通用编码智能体 Codex，并且在 41 个操作中的 34 个上优于其自身没有规则引导的变体。

paragraphs.en: C remains widely used in systems and performance-critical software for its low-level control, predictable performance, and minimal runtime overhead [ 1 , 2 ] . However, it is prone to memory-safety errors such as buffer overflows and use-after-free, which remain a major source of systems-software vulnerabilities [ 3 , 4 ] . Rust mitigates these risks through ownership and borrowing while retaining low-level performance [ 5 , 6 ] , which has motivated efforts to migrate legacy C codebases to Rust, including Rust support in the Linux kernel [ 7 ] . As manual migration is costly and error-prone, automated C-to-Rust translation has become an active research area [ 8 , 9 , 10 , 11 ] .
paragraphs.zh: C 语言因其底层控制能力、可预测的性能以及极小的运行时开销，在系统软件和性能关键型软件中仍被广泛使用 [ 1 , 2 ] 。 然而，它容易出现缓冲区溢出和释放后使用等内存安全错误，这些错误仍然是系统软件漏洞的主要来源 [ 3 , 4 ] 。 Rust 通过所有权和借用机制缓解了这些风险，同时保留了底层性能 [ 5 , 6 ] ，这推动了将遗留 C 代码库迁移到 Rust 的各项工作，包括在 Linux 内核中支持 Rust [ 7 ] 。 由于手动迁移成本高且容易出错，自动化的 C 到 Rust 翻译已成为一个活跃的研究领域 [ 8 , 9 , 10 , 11 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Existing approaches fall into two families. LLM-based translators aim to produce safer, more idiomatic Rust and increasingly use program analysis and project-level context to coordinate translations across components [ 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 ] . However, their outputs are not guaranteed to preserve behavior, a problem that worsens as project scale grows [ 13 , 17 , 12 , 14 ] . Rule-based transpilers such as c2rust instead apply deterministic syntax-directed rules that preserve source behavior, although their output retains C-oriented representations and extensive unsafe code [ 8 , 9 , 18 , 10 , 19 ] . Owing to this behavioral guarantee, rule-based output has become a common starting point for practical migration: it has been used in industrial projects [ 20 ] , and recent hybrid approaches refine c2rust -generated Rust with LLM-guided rewriting [ 21 , 22 , 23 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 现有方法分为两大类。 基于 LLM 的翻译器旨在生成更安全、更符合 Rust 惯用法的代码，并越来越多地使用程序分析和项目级上下文来协调跨组件的翻译 [ 12 , 13 , 14 , 15 , 16 ] 。 然而，它们的输出无法保证保持原有行为，且随着项目规模的增长，这一问题愈发严重 [ 13 , 17 , 12 , 14 ] 。 相比之下，c2rust 等基于规则的转译器采用确定性的语法导向规则来保持源代码行为，但其输出仍保留面向 C 的表示形式和大量的 unsafe 代码 [ 8 , 9 , 18 , 10 , 19 ] 。 由于这种行为保证，基于规则的输出已成为实际迁移工作的常见起点：它已被用于工业项目 [ 20 ] ，并且近期的混合方法利用 LLM 引导的重写来改进 c2rust 生成的 Rust 代码 [ 21 , 22 , 23 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Recently, the performance of translated code has drawn attention [ 24 , 25 , 26 ] . Behavioral preservation does not imply performance preservation, and regressions after migration can offset the benefits of Rust in performance-critical software, where runtime efficiency is often a key reason for using C. The concern is most direct in rule-based output, which retains many C-style code patterns [ 22 , 18 ] that can introduce runtime overhead. Xia et al. [ 24 ] evaluate c2rust -generated programs on a synthetic C corpus and identify Relooper-induced code duplication as one source of runtime overhead, and RUSTY [ 27 ] avoids this control-flow expansion through a specialized translation scheme. General-purpose optimizers such as SemOpt [ 28 ] and MoST [ 29 ] instead guide LLM-based rewriting with reusable optimization knowledge.

Consequently, three questions remain open: (1) whether and how much performance degrades after C-to-Rust translation in real-world projects ; (2) which execution costs and code-level mechanisms explain such degradation ; and (3) whether recurring mechanisms can be distilled into reusable rules for automated performance recovery .

paragraphs.en: To answer these questions, we conduct an empirical study of performance divergence in rule-based C-to-Rust translation using c2rust [ 8 ] , a transpiler widely adopted in research [ 10 , 30 ] and industry [ 20 ] . Its deterministic translation enables controlled paired C–Rust performance comparison. We construct a benchmark of 20 real-world C projects and their c2rust translations, using eight projects as the Study Dataset for empirical analysis and reserving the remaining twelve for evaluation. We measure performance at the granularity of operations , each being a complete program task with checkable output that may span multiple API calls, such as compression or decompression in bzip2 . Across 19 operations in the Study Dataset, the translated Rust incurs more than 3.0 % 3.0\% runtime overhead over C on 12, eight of which exceed 25.0 % 25.0\% with a maximum of 62.2 % 62.2\% . Execution-cost decomposition reveals three recurring profiles: additional dynamic instructions, higher cycles per instruction, or both. We trace these differences through optimized IR, compiler optimization remarks, and translated Rust source, identifying nine recurring performance issues. These issues span residual runtime work, missed compiler transformations, and recurring source-level patterns, each with a corresponding optimization direction.

paragraphs.en: Building on these findings, we present PerfR , a rule-guided framework for recovering performance lost during C-to-Rust migration. PerfR operationalizes each identified performance issue as an optimization guidance that pairs its Observed Pattern with the corresponding Optimization Direction . Given a C project, PerfR first obtains its unmodified c2rust translation (denoted RawRust ), constructs operation-level functional and performance workloads, and performs pre-optimization normalization. PerfR then localizes rule-specific issues in hot functions using optimized IR, compiler remarks, and Rust source. For each pattern group, the LLM evaluates rewrite preconditions against project context and synthesizes a candidate rewrite using the applicable optimization directions. Each candidate is accepted only if it preserves functionality and yields a net runtime improvement across the synthesized workloads.

paragraphs.en: C and Rust Compilation Pipelines. clang and rustc both use LLVM for optimization and machine-code generation, but their frontends can produce different LLVM IR from functionally equivalent C and Rust programs [ 31 , 32 ] . These differences arise from language-specific semantics and program representations. They affect both the work expressed in the IR and the information available to LLVM, potentially yielding machine code with different execution costs. LLVM provides two complementary artifacts for examining these differences. Optimized IR reveals what remains after optimization, while optimization remarks record selected transformations that LLVM performs or misses, with reasons when available, providing evidence about why optimization outcomes differ. Together, they support compiler-level analysis of C-to-Rust performance divergence.
paragraphs.zh: C 与 Rust 编译流水线。clang 和 rustc 都使用 LLVM 进行优化和机器码生成，但它们的前端可以从功能等价的 C 和 Rust 程序生成不同的 LLVM IR [31, 32]。 这些差异源于语言特定的语义和程序表示。 它们既影响 IR 中表达的工作，也影响 LLVM 可获得的信息，从而可能产生具有不同执行成本的机器码。 LLVM 提供了两个互补的产物用于检查这些差异。 优化后的 IR 揭示了优化之后留下什么，而优化备注记录了 LLVM 执行或错过的已选变换，并在可用时给出原因，为优化结果为何不同提供证据。 两者结合，支持对 C 到 Rust 性能差异的编译器层面分析。

paragraphs.en: Execution Performance Decomposition. For a fixed task and input, CPU execution time follows the performance equation T CPU = I × 𝐶𝑃𝐼 × T cycle T_{\mathrm{CPU}}=I\times\mathit{CPI}\times T_{\mathrm{cycle}} , where I I is the number of retired instructions, 𝐶𝑃𝐼 \mathit{CPI} is the average number of cycles per instruction, and T cycle T_{\mathrm{cycle}} is the duration of one clock cycle [ 33 ] . When implementations execute on the same processor under a fixed clock configuration, execution-cost differences can arise from instruction count, CPI, or both. Instruction count characterizes dynamic work, whereas CPI characterizes average per-instruction cost. Top-Down Microarchitecture Analysis (TMA) complements this decomposition with a hierarchical view of processor utilization. Its top-level categories are Retiring, Frontend Bound, Bad Speculation, and Backend Bound, with Backend Bound further divided into Core Bound and Memory Bound [ 34 ] . These categories help identify microarchitectural bottlenecks associated with CPI differences.

paragraphs.en: Project Selection. We construct the initial candidate pool from prior project-level C-to-Rust translation studies [ 10 , 9 , 35 , 25 , 13 , 21 , 36 ] . After deduplication, a project is eligible if it (i) contains at least 1 KLoC of project-owned C source and headers, excluding tests, examples, and dependencies; (ii) can be translated by c2rust into a functionally equivalent crate; and (iii) supports a deterministic workload exercising a measurable hotspot in project-owned code. We exclude projects whose execution is dominated by I/O or external libraries. These criteria yield 16 projects; to broaden external validity, we add four C libraries satisfying the same criteria: xxHash [ 37 ] , lz4 [ 38 ] , miniz [ 39 ] , and http-parser [ 40 ] . The resulting benchmark contains 20 projects ranging from 1 to 180 KLoC, partitioned into an eight-project Study Dataset for empirical analysis and performance-issue characterization and a disjoint twelve-project Evaluation Dataset for approach evaluation.

paragraphs.en: Operation Selection. We define an operation as a semantically complete end-to-end task that exercises a coherent unit of functionality, may span multiple APIs, and yields a checkable output. Operations provide a suitable granularity for performance comparison: project-level measurements are too coarse to distinguish functional paths, whereas API-level measurements are too fine-grained to represent complete functional tasks. We select an operation if it (i) represents core functionality, (ii) exercises a distinct performance-relevant implementation path, and (iii) can be executed on both C and the c2rust translation with outputs checked for equivalence. Multiple operations from the same project are retained only when they exercise distinct implementations. For example, we include both compression and decompression in bzip2 because exercise distinct implementation paths, and XXH64, XXH3, and XXH32 in xxHash because they implement distinct hashing algorithms.

paragraphs.en: Workload Inputs. For each benchmark operation, we prefer established corpora or upstream-provided inputs, such as the Silesia corpus [ 41 ] and the Native JSON Benchmark [ 42 ] . When suitable upstream inputs are unavailable, we generate inputs deterministically from fixed parameters so that the C implementation and its c2rust translation process identical data. For input-sensitive operations, we use multiple sizes or formats. For inverse operations, we generate the corresponding forward output once with the C reference and reuse it unchanged for both implementations. Overall, the workloads span upstream, generated, and derived inputs across multiple sizes and formats, while preserving identical inputs for each C–Rust comparison. The selected workloads achieve 73.0–100.0% coverage of reachable functions in each project.

paragraphs.en: Measurement Protocol. For each operation, corresponding C and Rust drivers invoke the respective implementations on the same workload input, and we measure them in pairs to obtain stable and directly comparable runtime estimates. When a single execution is too short for reliable timing, we use a fixed number of in-process repetitions to reach a minimum measurement duration, with the same repetition count for C and Rust. After warm-up, we collect paired measurements while alternating the C–Rust execution order across pairs to reduce temporal drift and order effects. We assess stability using the coefficient of variation (CV) of the pairwise Rust-to-C runtime ratios and repeat any unstable batch. For accepted batches, we remove ratio outliers using Tukey’s 1.5 × 1.5\times IQR rule [ 43 ] and report median runtimes. A pilot study on representative workloads showed that runtime estimates stabilized with a minimum measurement duration of 500 ms, five warm-up rounds, and 30 measurement pairs; we therefore use these settings throughout, consider a batch unstable when CV exceeds 3%, and allow at most two retries.
paragraphs.zh: 测量方法。 对于每个操作，对应的 C 与 Rust 驱动程序在同一工作负载输入上调用各自的实现，我们成对地对它们进行测量，以获得稳定且可直接比较的运行时间估计。 当单次执行时间过短而无法可靠计时的时候，我们使用固定的进程内重复次数来达到最小测量时长，且 C 和 Rust 使用相同的重复次数。 预热之后，我们收集成对的测量数据，并在各对之间交替 C–Rust 的执行顺序，以减少时间漂移和顺序效应。 我们使用成对的 Rust 与 C 运行时间比值的变异系数（CV）来评估稳定性，并对任何不稳定的批次进行重测。 对于被接受的批次，我们使用 Tukey 的 1.5 × IQR 规则 [ 43 ] 去除比值中的离群值，并报告运行时间的中位数。 一项针对代表性工作负载的试点研究表明，当最小测量时长为 500 ms、预热轮数为五轮、测量对数为 30 对时，运行时间估计趋于稳定；因此我们在全文中采用这些设置，当 CV 超过 3% 时判定该批次不稳定，并允许最多重试两次。

paragraphs.en: Optimized IR. We compare whole-program optimized IR of C and its c2rust translation. paragraphs.en: We analyze the evidence in three steps. First, we record each performance-relevant candidate instance with its source region in the translated Rust, its manifestation in IR, compiler remarks, or source code, and its cost mechanism. Evidence from multiple representations referring to the same source construct and mechanism is merged. We then discard candidates whose code is not exercised by the workload (58) or belongs to the benchmark harness rather than the project (14), whose evidence does not support the stated mechanism (48), or whose C–Rust difference disappears in optimized IR (15). Of 404 candidates, 269 are retained as instances . Second, we group instances that share an underlying performance mechanism and admit a common remediation strategy. We retain only groups supported by at least three instances; each retained group defines a Performance Issue . This yields nine issues covering 268 of the 269 instances. The remaining instance concerns a state variable introduced by c2rust to emulate goto ; observed in only one function, it falls below the support threshold. Third, for each retained issue, we abstract its recurring manifestations into an Observed Pattern and derive an Optimization Direction targeting the underlying mechanism. For issues identified through IR or compiler remarks, we use paired C–Rust evidence to determine how to eliminate extra work absent from C or restore optimizations realized in C. For source-level issues, we map the underlying mechanism to a recommendation in The Rust Performance Book [ 44 ] , such as reusing a buffer across calls rather than allocating and freeing it on every call.

paragraphs.en: Residual Runtime Work. Optimized IR reveals two recurring forms of residual work in translated Rust: Residual Bounds Checks and Redundant Conversion Saturation . Residual Bounds Checks persist despite provably valid access ranges. In BZ2_decompress , a nested traversal writes (*s).inUse[(i * 16 + j) as usize] , where i < 16 and j < 16 guarantee an index below 256. Yet the Rust IR retains a comparison against 256 and a branch to panic_bounds_check , while the corresponding C IR has no such failure path. The translated state-machine control flow prevents LLVM from recovering this range invariant. Expressing the traversal over a bounded slice makes the valid extent explicit and enables the redundant check to be eliminated. Redundant Conversion Saturation persists when operand ranges rule out saturation but the Rust IR retains saturating float-to-integer conversions. In heman , seven such conversions originate from fastFloor after inlining into heman_internal_generate_island_noise . The Rust IR uses llvm.fptosi.sat or llvm.fptoui.sat , whereas the corresponding C IR uses direct fptosi or fptoui . The operands are finite grid coordinates whose truncated values remain within the target integer range. Once these conditions are established, to_int_unchecked eliminates the redundant saturation.

paragraphs.en: Missed Compiler Transformations. Paired C–Rust compiler remarks reveal two recurring missed transformations in translated Rust: Missed Loop Vectorization and Missed Hot-Callee Inlining . The Missed Loop Vectorization issue occurs when LLVM vectorizes a C loop but leaves its translated Rust counterpart scalar. In bzip2 , five hot decode loops exhibit this divergence. In a representative move-to-front loop that shifts mtfa entries, each array access carries a bounds check that adds a loop exit, and LLVM reports that it could not determine the number of loop iterations. Expressing the shift as a bounded slice operation can remove these checks and enable vectorization. The Missed Hot-Callee Inlining issue occurs when a hot call inlined in C remains uninlined in translated Rust because of missing inlining attributes or excessive estimated callee cost. In xxHash , the C implementation forces XXH3_accumulate_512_scalar to inline, whereas its translated Rust counterpart lacks the corresponding annotation and retains the call inside the hot stripe-processing loop. Restoring the missing inlining annotation can eliminate this barrier.
paragraphs.zh: 编译器漏失的转换。 成对的 C–Rust 编译器提示揭示了翻译后 Rust 中两种反复出现的漏失转换：循环向量化的漏失与热 callee 内联的漏失。 循环向量化漏失问题发生在 LLVM 对某个 C 循环进行了向量化，却让其翻译后的 Rust 对应循环保持标量形式时。 在 bzip2 中，有五个热点解码循环表现出这种分歧。 在一个移动 mtfa 条目的代表性 move-to-front 循环中，每次数组访问都带有一次边界检查，从而增加了一个循环出口，并且 LLVM 报告其无法确定循环迭代次数。 将该移位操作表达为有界切片（slice）运算可以移除这些检查并启用向量化。 热 callee 内联漏失问题发生在 C 中被内联的热点调用在翻译后的 Rust 中因缺少内联属性或估计的 callee 成本过高而未被内联时。 在 xxHash 中，C 实现强制将 XXH3_accumulate_512_scalar 内联，而其翻译后的 Rust 对应实现缺少相应的注解，并在热点 stripe 处理循环内保留了该调用。 恢复缺失的内联注解即可消除这一障碍。

paragraphs.en: Recurring Source-Level Patterns. Source inspection identifies five patterns in translated Rust code: Repeated Invariant Dispatch , Inefficient Buffer Management , Byte-Oriented Memory Operations , Scalar Element-Wise Processing , and Obscured Memory Access Properties . Unlike residual runtime work and missed compiler transformations, these patterns are characterized primarily by recurring source structures and their associated cost mechanisms. For example, Inefficient Buffer Management occurs in libzahl , where zmul_ll creates and releases four temporary integers at every recursion level, resizing their storage through libzahl_realloc when needed. Reusing preallocated scratch storage across recursive calls avoids this repeated allocation and resizing overhead.
paragraphs.zh: 反复出现的源码级模式。 源码检查在翻译后的 Rust 代码中识别出五种模式：重复的不变量分发、低效的缓冲区管理、面向字节的内存操作、标量逐元素处理，以及被掩盖的内存访问属性。 与残留的运行时工作和错失的编译器转换不同，这些模式的主要特征是反复出现的源码结构及其相关的开销机制。 例如，低效的缓冲区管理出现在 libzahl 中，其中 zmul_ll 在每一层递归都会创建并释放四个临时整数，并在需要时通过 libzahl_realloc 调整它们的存储大小。 在递归调用中复用预分配的暂存存储可以避免这种反复的分配和调整大小开销。

paragraphs.en: The Obscured Memory Access Properties issue arises when raw-pointer accesses leave bounds and aliasing relationships implicit, limiting LLVM’s ability to eliminate redundant loads. In libzahl , zrsh traverses limb arrays through raw-pointer accesses such as *ptr.offset(i) . The optimized Rust IR contains 73 static load instructions, compared with 24 in C, and lacks the !tbaa metadata present in the C IR. Consistently, GVN emits 46 missed-optimization remarks for Rust, versus 16 for C, frequently citing potentially aliasing writes as barriers to load elimination. Together, these observations suggest that obscured access relationships lead to conservative memory-dependence assumptions that inhibit load reuse. Recovering valid &[T] / &mut [T] views can expose these properties to LLVM and enable load elimination.

paragraphs.en: The performance issues derived in § IV-C provide reusable guidance for recovering translation-induced performance loss. Applying this guidance to a new project requires localizing performance-critical code and identifying applicable rules. We therefore present PerfR , a rule-guided framework for recovering performance lost during C-to-Rust migration. Starting from a C project, PerfR obtains RawRust with c2rust , synthesizes workloads, and performs pre-optimization normalization (Figure 1 ). PerfR then localizes hot functions, identifies applicable optimization rules, and uses project context to guide precondition-aware LLM rewrites. Each rewrite is accepted only if it preserves functionality and improves performance.
paragraphs.zh: 第IV-C节中推导出的性能问题为恢复翻译导致的性能损失提供了可复用的指导。 将该指导应用于新项目需要定位性能关键代码并确定适用的规则。 因此，我们提出了PerfR，一个用于恢复C到Rust迁移过程中损失的性能的规则引导框架。 PerfR从C项目出发，使用c2rust获得RawRust，合成工作负载，并执行预优化归一化（图1）。 随后，PerfR定位热点函数，识别适用的优化规则，并利用项目上下文引导具备前置条件感知的智能体重写。 每次重写只有在保留功能且提升性能时才会被接受。

paragraphs.en: Project-level optimization requires executable workloads to locate runtime hotspots and evaluate candidate rewrites. To capture end-to-end behavior and cost, PerfR organizes these workloads around operations that compose related APIs into complete tasks with checkable outputs. Starting from RawRust , PerfR synthesizes executable operations and harnesses and refines them using coverage feedback. This shared execution basis supports two complementary workload types: functional workloads provide diverse inputs for regression testing, while performance workloads provide sufficiently long executions for hotspot localization and performance validation. These internal workloads are independent of the benchmark workloads used for final evaluation.

paragraphs.en: Operation and Harness Synthesis. PerfR first extracts the public API of RawRust , including pub functions and structs together with their module paths, and provides this information to the LLM. The LLM plans a bounded set of end-to-end operations, each representing a distinct functional task and identifying the API elements needed to realize it. Planning prioritizes core functionality and broad public-function coverage across the operation set.
paragraphs.zh: 操作与测试框架合成。 PerfR 首先提取 RawRust 的公开 API，包括 pub 函数和结构体及其模块路径，并将这些信息提供给大语言模型。 大语言模型规划出一组有界的端到端操作，每个操作代表一个独立的功能任务，并识别实现该任务所需的 API 元素。 规划优先考虑核心功能，并在操作集上实现广泛的公开函数覆盖。

paragraphs.en: The planned operations, however, are not directly executable. For each operation, the LLM uses the associated API signatures to generate an executable harness and a small set of distinct seed inputs. The harness invokes the relevant APIs for each seed and produces an observable output. PerfR compiles and repeatedly executes the harness to check successful execution and output determinism. It also checks for output variation across distinct seeds to reject degenerate harnesses that ignore their inputs. When a check fails, the corresponding diagnostic feedback is returned to the LLM for revision [ 13 , 45 ] . This process continues within a fixed repair budget, and an operation is retained only when its harness passes all checks.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，计划好的操作并不能直接执行。 对于每个操作，大语言模型使用相关联的 API 签名生成一个可执行的测试装置（harness）以及一小组不同的种子输入。 该测试装置为每个种子调用相关 API，并产生可观测的输出。 PerfR 编译并反复执行该测试装置，以检查执行是否成功以及输出是否具有确定性。 它还检查不同种子之间的输出是否存在差异，以拒绝那些忽略其输入的退化测试装置。 当某项检查失败时，相应的诊断反馈会返回给大语言模型进行修订 [ 13 , 45 ] 。 该过程在固定的修复预算内持续进行，只有当某个操作的测试装置通过所有检查时，该操作才会被保留。

sents.zh: 然而，计划好的操作并不能直接执行。

sents.zh: 该测试装置为每个种子调用相关 API，并产生可观测的输出。

sents.zh: PerfR 编译并反复执行该测试装置，以检查执行是否成功以及输出是否具有确定性。

sents.en: It also checks for output variation across distinct seeds to reject degenerate harnesses that ignore their inputs.
sents.zh: 它还检查不同种子之间的输出是否存在差异，以拒绝那些忽略其输入的退化测试装置。

sents.zh: 当某项检查失败时，相应的诊断反馈会返回给大语言模型进行修订 [ 13 , 45 ] 。

paragraphs.en: Executability alone, however, does not ensure broad coverage of the public API. PerfR therefore measures public-function coverage across the retained operations using an instrumented build and their seed inputs. If coverage remains below the target, the uncovered functions and their signatures are provided to the LLM, which extends existing operations or introduces new ones. The harnesses and seed inputs are then generated and validated through the same process before coverage is recomputed. This feedback loop continues until the coverage target is reached or the refinement budget is exhausted, yielding the final operation set and validated harnesses.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，仅具备可执行性并不能确保对公开 API 的广泛覆盖。 因此，PerfR 使用插桩构建版本和种子输入，来衡量保留操作对公开函数的覆盖情况。 如果覆盖率仍低于目标，未覆盖的函数及其签名将被提供给大语言模型，由其扩展现有操作或引入新操作。 然后生成测试驱动程序和种子输入，并通过相同流程进行验证，之后重新计算覆盖率。 该反馈循环持续进行，直到达到覆盖率目标或精炼预算耗尽，最终产出最终的操作集合和经过验证的测试驱动程序。

paragraphs.en: Functional Workload Synthesis. The validated harnesses establish operation executability, but their small seed sets provide limited behavioral diversity for regression testing. PerfR therefore fuzzes the seeds of each retained operation to generate a broader input corpus. Each generated input is executed repeatedly on the initial RawRust . Inputs that fail or produce nondeterministic outputs are discarded, while stable output digests are recorded as regression references. The retained inputs, their reference digests, and the corresponding harness together form the functional workload used to validate subsequent rewrites.
paragraphs.zh: 功能工作负载合成。 经过验证的测试工具确立了操作的可执行性，但其较小的种子集为回归测试提供的行为多样性有限。 因此，PerfR 对每个保留操作的种子进行模糊测试，以生成更广泛的输入语料库。 每个生成的输入都会在初始的 RawRust 上重复执行。 失败或产生非确定性输出的输入会被丢弃，而稳定的输出摘要则被记录为回归参考。 保留的输入、其参考摘要以及对应的测试工具共同构成了用于验证后续重写的功能工作负载。

paragraphs.en: Performance Workload Synthesis. Functional workloads prioritize input diversity, but individual executions may be too short for reliable performance measurement. PerfR therefore constructs a separate performance input for each operation by scaling a semantically meaningful input dimension, such as record count, data size, or image dimensions. For operations that consume derived formats, PerfR scales the source data and invokes the corresponding producer operation to construct a valid input. If a single execution remains too short for stable timing, PerfR calibrates a fixed number of in-process repetitions to reach a minimum measurement duration. The harness, performance input, and repetition count together define a performance workload used for hotspot localization and performance validation. The operation budget, coverage target, refinement budget, and timing parameters are specified in the experimental setup.
paragraphs.zh: 性能负载合成。 功能性负载优先考虑输入多样性，但单次执行可能过短，无法进行可靠的性能测量。 因此，PerfR 通过放大具有语义意义的输入维度（例如记录数量、数据大小或图像尺寸）来为每个操作构造独立的性能输入。 对于消费派生格式的操作，PerfR 会缩放源数据并调用相应的生产者操作来构造有效输入。 如果单次执行仍因过短而无法获得稳定的计时，PerfR 会校准一个固定的进程内重复次数，以达到最小测量时长。 测试框架、性能输入与重复次数共同定义了一个性能负载，用于热点定位和性能验证。 操作预算、覆盖目标、精化预算和计时参数均在实验设置中给出说明。

paragraphs.en: Given a C project, c2rust yields RawRust , which preserves the behavior of the C program. However, RawRust retains C-oriented representations, including duplicated definitions, internal extern ‘‘C’’ boundaries, and pervasive raw-pointer accesses. Although these representations are not the performance issues identified in § IV-C , they hinder project-wide analysis and coordinated rewriting while obscuring optimization-relevant program properties. PerfR performs a preparatory refinement that consolidates shared definitions and refines internal ABI, pointer, and safety boundaries. Each refinement is validated against § V-A functional workloads; failing changes are reverted.
paragraphs.zh: 给定一个 C 项目，c2rust 会生成 RawRust，它保留了 C 程序的行为。 然而，RawRust 保留了面向 C 的表示，包括重复的定义、内部的 extern “C” 边界，以及普遍存在的裸指针访问。 尽管这些表示并不是第 IV-C 节中 identified 的性能问题，但它们阻碍了项目级分析和协同重写，同时掩盖了与优化相关的程序属性。 PerfR 执行一项预备性的精化，即整合共享定义并精化内部 ABI、指针和安全边界。 每项精化都针对第 V-A 节的功能性工作负载进行验证；未通过验证的更改会被回退。

sents.zh: 给定一个 C 项目，c2rust 会生成 RawRust，它保留了 C 程序的行为。

paragraphs.en: Declarations from shared C headers may appear as duplicate definitions across translated Rust modules. PerfR collects top-level items, including nominal types, type aliases, constants, statics, and functions, and groups them by source provenance. Definitions are compared after ignoring comments and formatting whitespace; attributes, declared types, and item bodies remain part of the comparison. Items originating from the same C declaration with identical normalized definitions form candidate groups. Static definitions remain separate to preserve storage identity. Function consolidation additionally requires consistent resolved dependencies and compatible linkage semantics. Eligible groups are processed in dependency order. For each group, PerfR retains one canonical definition in a shared module and replaces the remaining copies with imports.
paragraphs.zh: 来自共享 C 头文件的声明可能在多个已翻译的 Rust 模块中表现为重复定义。 PerfR 收集顶层项，包括名义类型、类型别名、常量、静态项和函数，并按来源出处对它们进行分组。 定义在忽略注释和格式化空白后进行比较；属性、声明的类型以及项的主体仍作为比较的一部分。 来自同一 C 声明且具有相同规范化定义的项构成候选组。 静态定义保持独立，以保留存储标识。 函数合并还需要已解析的依赖项保持一致以及链接语义兼容。 符合条件的组按依赖顺序处理。 对于每个组，PerfR 在共享模块中保留一个规范定义，并用导入替换其余副本。

sents.en: Declarations from shared C headers may appear as duplicate definitions across translated Rust modules.
sents.zh: 来自共享 C 头文件的声明可能在多个已翻译的 Rust 模块中表现为重复定义。

sents.zh: 来自同一 C 声明且具有相同规范化定义的项构成候选组。

sents.en: Static definitions remain separate to preserve storage identity.
sents.zh: 静态定义保持独立，以保留存储标识。

sents.en: Function consolidation additionally requires consistent resolved dependencies and compatible linkage semantics.
sents.zh: 函数合并还需要已解析的依赖项保持一致以及链接语义兼容。

sents.en: Eligible groups are processed in dependency order.
sents.zh: 符合条件的组按依赖顺序处理。

sents.zh: 对于每个组，PerfR 在共享模块中保留一个规范定义，并用导入替换其余副本。

paragraphs.en: Internal ABI Recovery. After definition consolidation, PerfR examines each project-defined extern "C" function to determine whether the C ABI remains necessary. The boundary is preserved when the function participates in an external interface or is used through a C-ABI function pointer. When all uses are project-local, PerfR removes extern "C" and #[no_mangle] , removes the corresponding external declarations, and rewrites callers to invoke the function directly through its Rust module path.
paragraphs.zh: 内部 ABI 恢复。 在定义合并之后，PerfR 会检查每个项目定义的 extern "C" 函数，以判断 C ABI 是否仍然必要。 当该函数参与外部接口，或通过 C-ABI 函数指针被使用时，该边界会被保留。 当所有使用都是项目内部的时，PerfR 会移除 extern "C" 和 #[no_mangle]，删除对应的外部声明，并重写调用方，使其通过该函数的 Rust 模块路径直接调用它。

sents.en: Internal ABI Recovery.
sents.zh: 内部 ABI 恢复。

sents.en: After definition consolidation, PerfR examines each project-defined extern "C" function to determine whether the C ABI remains necessary.
sents.zh: 在定义合并之后，PerfR 会检查每个项目定义的 extern "C" 函数，以判断 C ABI 是否仍然必要。

sents.en: The boundary is preserved when the function participates in an external interface or is used through a C-ABI function pointer.
sents.zh: 当该函数参与外部接口，或通过 C-ABI 函数指针被使用时，该边界会被保留。

sents.en: When all uses are project-local, PerfR removes extern "C" and #[no_mangle] , removes the corresponding external declarations, and rewrites callers to invoke the function directly through its Rust module path.
sents.zh: 当所有使用都是项目内部的时，PerfR 会移除 extern "C" 和 #[no_mangle]，删除对应的外部声明，并重写调用方，使其通过该函数的 Rust 模块路径直接调用它。

paragraphs.en: Local Pointer-View Recovery. After restoring internal Rust call relationships, function bodies may still access objects and buffers through raw-pointer parameters. Following the pointer-semantics recovery strategy of prior C-to-Rust translation work [ 13 ] , PerfR analyzes each raw-pointer parameter to determine whether its accesses can be represented by a Rust reference or slice. For a pointer to an individual object, it constructs a local &T or &mut T view; for a contiguous buffer, it recovers the accessed extent and constructs &[T] or &mut [T] . Shared views require no conflicting writes, while mutable views additionally require exclusive access. When these conditions cannot be established, the raw-pointer representation is retained; otherwise, covered dereferences and pointer-offset accesses are rewritten through the recovered view.
paragraphs.zh: 局部指针视图恢复。 在恢复内部的 Rust 调用关系之后，函数体仍可能通过裸指针参数访问对象和缓冲区。 遵循此前 C 到 Rust 翻译工作的指针语义恢复策略 [ 13 ]，PerfR 分析每个裸指针参数，以判断其访问能否用 Rust 引用或切片来表示。 对于指向单个对象的指针，它会构造一个局部 &T 或 &mut T 视图；对于连续缓冲区，它会恢复被访问的范围并构造 &[T] 或 &mut [T]。 共享视图要求不存在冲突写入，而可变视图还额外要求独占访问。 当这些条件无法成立时，将保留裸指针表示；否则，被覆盖的解引用和指针偏移访问将通过恢复出的视图进行重写。

sents.zh: 局部指针视图恢复。

sents.zh: 对于指向单个对象的指针，它会构造一个局部 &T 或 &mut T 视图；对于连续缓冲区，它会恢复被访问的范围并构造 &[T] 或 &mut [T]。

paragraphs.en: Unsafe-Boundary Narrowing. Recovering references and slices reduces the code requiring an unsafe context but may leave caller-side safety obligations. PerfR therefore reassesses each function-level unsafe annotation. The unsafe fn marker is retained when callers must uphold safety preconditions that cannot be established within the function, such as raw-pointer validity. Otherwise, PerfR removes the marker and confines unsafe operations to local unsafe blocks; blocks reported as unused_unsafe by the compiler are then removed.
paragraphs.zh: 不安全边界收窄。 恢复引用和切片可减少需要不安全上下文的代码，但可能留下调用方侧的安全义务。 因此，PerfR 会重新评估每个函数级的不安全标注。 当调用方必须遵守无法在函数内部建立的安全前置条件（例如裸指针的有效性）时，则保留 unsafe fn 标记。 否则，PerfR 移除该标记，并将不安全操作限制在局部的 unsafe 块中；随后，被编译器报告为 unused_unsafe 的块将被移除。

sents.zh: 不安全边界收窄。

sents.zh: 因此，PerfR 会重新评估每个函数级的不安全标注。

sents.en: The unsafe fn marker is retained when callers must uphold safety preconditions that cannot be established within the function, such as raw-pointer validity.
sents.zh: 当调用方必须遵守无法在函数内部建立的安全前置条件（例如裸指针的有效性）时，则保留 unsafe fn 标记。

sents.en: Otherwise, PerfR removes the marker and confines unsafe operations to local unsafe blocks; blocks reported as unused_unsafe by the compiler are then removed.
sents.zh: 否则，PerfR 移除该标记，并将不安全操作限制在局部的 unsafe 块中；随后，被编译器报告为 unused_unsafe 的块将被移除。

paragraphs.en: Project-level performance optimization requires answering two questions: where optimization can materially affect end-to-end runtime, and what performance issues should be addressed there. PerfR first profiles the performance workloads to localize project-owned hot functions. PerfR then uses the Observed Pattern and corresponding Optimization Direction derived for each recurring issue in RQ3 (§ IV-C ) to identify concrete optimization targets within these functions. PerfR therefore first localizes hot functions and then matches these patterns against their optimized IR, compiler remarks, and Rust source to identify concrete optimization targets.
paragraphs.zh: 项目级性能优化需要回答两个问题：优化在哪里能显著影响端到端运行时间，以及在那里应该解决哪些性能问题。 PerfR 首先对性能工作负载进行剖析，以定位项目自身拥有的热点函数。 PerfR 然后使用 RQ3（§ IV-C）中为每个反复出现的问题推导出的观察模式及对应的优化方向，来识别这些函数中的具体优化目标。 因此，PerfR 首先定位热点函数，然后将这些模式与其优化后的 IR、编译器备注以及 Rust 源代码进行匹配，以识别具体的优化目标。

paragraphs.en: Project-level optimization need not examine every function equally, since optimizing code with little runtime contribution yields limited end-to-end benefit [ 46 , 47 ] . Amdahl’s law further quantifies this limitation [ 48 ] : eliminating the execution cost of a region accounting for a runtime fraction p p yields a speedup of at most 1 / ( 1 − p ) 1/(1-p) . PerfR therefore localizes project-owned hot functions for subsequent optimization.
paragraphs.zh: 项目级优化无需同等审视每个函数，因为优化运行时贡献很小的代码只能带来有限的端到端收益 [ 46 , 47 ] 。 阿姆达尔定律进一步量化了这一局限 [ 48 ] ：若消除一个占运行时比例为 p p 的区域的执行开销，加速比至多为 1 / ( 1 − p ) 1/(1-p) 。 因此，PerfR 会定位项目自有的热点函数，以供后续优化。

paragraphs.en: To identify these functions, PerfR profiles each performance workload using perf , collecting cycle samples together with their call stacks, and attributes each sample to a project-owned function. Attribution by machine-code symbol is unreliable for translated code: small project functions are often inlined into their callers, including the harness, and some project functions delegate their work to C library routines. In both cases, the samples would be charged to code other than the function that should be rewritten. PerfR therefore expands inlined frames using debug information and attributes each sample to the deepest project-owned frame on its call stack. For samples in project-owned code, attribution to the deepest project-owned frame prevents callers from appearing hot because of expensive project callees. Samples in non-project code, such as C library routines, are instead attributed to the invoking project function, which is the actionable rewrite target. Let s ⁡ ( f , w ) s(f,w) denote the fraction of cycle samples attributed to project-owned function f f under workload w w , referred to as its attributed cycle share . Because hotspots may vary across workloads, PerfR defines project-level hotness as h ⁡ ( f ) = max w ∈ 𝒲 perf ⁡ s ⁡ ( f , w ) h(f)=\max_{w\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{perf}}}s(f,w) , where 𝒲 perf \mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{perf}} is the set of performance workloads. Taking the maximum preserves workload-specific hotspots that would be diluted by averaging across workloads. PerfR ranks functions by h ⁡ ( f ) h(f) , discards those below the hotness threshold, and retains up to a fixed budget of the highest-ranked functions, yielding ℋ = { f 1 , f 2 , … , f n } \mathcal{H}=\{f_{1},f_{2},\ldots,f_{n}\} .
paragraphs.zh: 为了识别这些函数，PerfR 使用 perf 对每个性能工作负载进行剖析，收集周期采样及其调用栈，并将每个采样归因于项目自有的函数。 基于机器码符号的归因对经过转换的代码并不可靠：小的项目函数通常会被内联到其调用者（包括测试框架）中，而且一些项目函数会将工作委托给 C 库例程。 在这两种情况下，采样都会被计到本应被重写函数之外的其他代码上。 因此，PerfR 利用调试信息展开内联的栈帧，并将每个采样归因于其调用栈中最深的项目自有栈帧。 对于位于项目自有代码中的采样，归因于最深的项目自有栈帧可以避免调用者因高开销的项目被调用函数而显得热点。 位于非项目代码（例如 C 库例程）中的采样则被归因于调用它的项目函数，因为该函数才是可操作的重写目标。 设 s ⁡ ( f , w ) s(f,w) 表示在工作负载 w w 下归因于项目自有函数 f f 的周期采样比例，称为其归因周期份额。 由于热点可能因工作负载而异，PerfR 将项目级热度定义为 h ⁡ ( f ) = max w ∈ 𝒲 perf ⁡ s ⁡ ( f , w ) h(f)=\max_{w\in\mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{perf}}}s(f,w) ，其中 𝒲 perf \mathcal{W}_{\mathrm{perf}} 是性能工作负载的集合。 取最大值可以保留工作负载特定的热点，否则这些热点在跨工作负载取平均时会被稀释。 PerfR 按 h ⁡ ( f ) h(f) 对函数排序，丢弃低于热度阈值的函数，并保留排名最高的至多固定预算数量的函数，得到 ℋ = { f 1 , f 2 , … , f n } \mathcal{H}=\{f_{1},f_{2},\ldots,f_{n}\} 。

paragraphs.en: Hotspot localization identifies which functions should be prioritized for optimization, but not the concrete performance issues within them. We encode each performance issue identified in RQ3 (§ IV-C ) as an optimization rule pairing its Observed Pattern with the corresponding Optimization Direction . The former defines the matching criteria for identifying issue occurrences, while the latter guides subsequent rewriting. PerfR realizes the matching criteria through three analyzers over optimized IR, compiler remarks, and Rust source. Although some patterns are derived using paired C–Rust evidence, matching relies only on Rust-side artifacts.

paragraphs.en: Optimization Remarks Analyzer. PerfR compiles the project with optimization remarks enabled and matches remarks by their reporting pass and reason against the corresponding Observed Pattern . Only remarks whose reported barriers conform to the corresponding Observed Pattern are retained. For example, vectorization remarks reporting insufficient profitability are excluded, while inlining matches additionally require the call to remain in optimized IR. GVN and LICM remarks attributing failed load elimination or hoisting to potentially clobbering stores are candidate matches for Obscured Memory Access Properties .

paragraphs.en: Rust Source Analyzer. PerfR parses the project into syntax trees and builds a project-wide symbol index resolving types, globals, functions, and caller–callee relationships. These representations enable structural matching of the source-level Observed Patterns . For example, a buffer that is repeatedly allocated and released or grown by fixed increments through realloc is a candidate match for Inefficient Buffer Management .
paragraphs.zh: Rust 源代码分析器。 PerfR 将项目解析为语法树，并构建项目级的符号索引，解析类型、全局变量、函数以及调用者—被调用者关系。 这些表示使得对源码层面的观察模式（Observed Patterns）进行结构化匹配成为可能。 例如，通过 realloc 反复分配和释放或按固定增量增长的缓冲区，就是低效缓冲区管理（Inefficient Buffer Management）的候选匹配。

paragraphs.en: Applying these analyzers yields candidate occurrences of the identified performance issues, each associated with a matched rule and a source location. Because the three analyzers report locations in different forms, PerfR normalizes them before further processing: IR matches are mapped through debug metadata and inline-call chains, optimization remarks provide compiler-reported locations, and source matches directly identify syntax-tree ranges. PerfR then converts these locations to project-relative source ranges, associates each match with its enclosing source function, and retains only matches within the hot-function set ℋ \mathcal{H} . To remove duplicate matches and form coherent rewrite regions, PerfR consolidates the retained matches in two stages. First, matches that associate the same rule with the same source construct, including those from different analyzers, are merged into a single pattern instance . Second, co-located instances are combined into a pattern group when their source regions overlap, nest, or occur in nearby statements of the same block, subject to a bound on the enclosing region size; otherwise, an instance forms a singleton group. Each group is anchored at the smallest enclosing syntactic region covering its instances, such as an expression, a statement sequence, or a loop.
paragraphs.zh: 应用这些分析器后会得到所识别性能问题的候选出现位置，每个候选位置都与一条匹配规则和一个源代码位置相关联。 由于三个分析器报告的位置形式各不相同，PerfR 在进一步处理之前会先对它们进行规范化：IR 匹配通过调试元数据和内联调用链进行映射，优化备注提供编译器报告的位置，而源代码匹配则直接标识语法树范围。 随后，PerfR 将这些位置转换为相对于项目的源代码范围，将每个匹配与其所在的源函数关联起来，并仅保留位于热点函数集合 ℋ \mathcal{H} 内的匹配。 为了去除重复匹配并形成连贯的重写区域，PerfR 分两个阶段对保留的匹配进行合并。 首先，将同一条规则关联到同一源代码构造的匹配（包括来自不同分析器的匹配）合并为一个单一的模式实例。 其次，当多个实例的源区域相互重叠、嵌套，或出现在同一代码块的相邻语句中时，在限定所含区域大小上限的前提下，将这些共置实例合并为一个模式组；否则，该实例单独构成一个单例组。 每个组都锚定在覆盖其所有实例的最小封闭语法区域上，例如一个表达式、一个语句序列或一个循环。

sents.en: To remove duplicate matches and form coherent rewrite regions, PerfR consolidates the retained matches in two stages.
sents.zh: 为了去除重复匹配并形成连贯的重写区域，PerfR 分两个阶段对保留的匹配进行合并。

sents.en: First, matches that associate the same rule with the same source construct, including those from different analyzers, are merged into a single pattern instance .
sents.zh: 首先，将同一条规则关联到同一源代码构造的匹配（包括来自不同分析器的匹配）合并为一个单一的模式实例。

sents.en: Second, co-located instances are combined into a pattern group when their source regions overlap, nest, or occur in nearby statements of the same block, subject to a bound on the enclosing region size; otherwise, an instance forms a singleton group.
sents.zh: 其次，当多个实例的源区域相互重叠、嵌套，或出现在同一代码块的相邻语句中时，在限定所含区域大小上限的前提下，将这些共置实例合并为一个模式组；否则，该实例单独构成一个单例组。

sents.en: Each group is anchored at the smallest enclosing syntactic region covering its instances, such as an expression, a statement sequence, or a loop.
sents.zh: 每个组都锚定在覆盖其所有实例的最小封闭语法区域上，例如一个表达式、一个语句序列或一个循环。

paragraphs.en: For each hot function f ∈ ℋ f\in\mathcal{H} , PerfR represents the resulting groups as M f = { ⟨ ℓ i , R i ⟩ } i = 1 m f , M_{f}=\{\langle\ell_{i},R_{i}\rangle\}_{i=1}^{m_{f}}, where m f m_{f} is the number of candidate optimization regions in f f , ℓ i \ell_{i} is the source region of the i i -th group, and R i R_{i} is its set of matched optimization rules. Each pair therefore specifies where to rewrite and which optimization directions to consider jointly. For example, a residual bounds-check match at an indexed expression and a vectorization-failure match at its enclosing loop may be grouped at the loop level. The resulting group contains both Residual Bounds Checks and Missed Loop Vectorization , allowing their optimization directions to be coordinated in a single rewrite. These groups form the units for subsequent optimization.

A match, however, only indicates that the corresponding Optimization Direction may be relevant; applying that direction requires rewrite-specific semantic preconditions that the Observed Pattern alone does not establish. To make these requirements explicit, PerfR augments each rule with rewrite preconditions . These preconditions, together with the Observed Pattern and Optimization Direction , form an optimization card . The LLM agent then evaluates these preconditions at the matched region before synthesizing a candidate rewrite.

paragraphs.en: For each concrete rewrite form associated with an Optimization Direction , we identify the semantic obligations required to preserve the behavior of the original code. These obligations follow from established legality conditions for the corresponding program transformation where applicable [ 49 , 50 ] ; otherwise, they are derived from the behavioral-equivalence requirements of the rewrite. When a rewrite introduces a Rust construct or API, we additionally incorporate its documented validity requirements [ 51 ] . For example, Figure 2 illustrates mutable-slice recovery for Obscured Memory Access Properties : the corresponding card requires establishing the buffer extent, ensuring that accesses remain within that extent, and excluding conflicting accesses while the mutable slice is live. We express these obligations as concrete checks over the target code, forming the card’s rewrite-precondition checklist .
paragraphs.zh: 对于与优化方向相关联的每种具体重写形式，我们识别出保持原始代码行为所需的语义义务。 这些义务在适用的情况下遵循相应程序变换的既定合法性条件 [49, 50]；否则，它们从该重写的行为等价性要求中推导得出。 当重写引入某个 Rust 构造或 API 时，我们还会纳入其文档中记录的有效性要求 [51]。 例如，图 2 展示了针对「被混淆的内存访问属性」的可变切片恢复：对应的卡片要求确定缓冲区范围、确保访问保持在该范围内，并在可变切片存活期间排除冲突访问。 我们将这些义务表述为对目标代码的具体检查，构成卡片的重写前置条件清单。

paragraphs.en: To enable the LLM to assess the rewrite-precondition checklist, PerfR provides the program context needed to establish the required conditions. For each pattern group ⟨ ℓ i , ℛ i ⟩ ∈ M f \langle\ell_{i},\mathcal{R}_{i}\rangle\in M_{f} , PerfR instantiates the associated optimization cards as matched optimization cards by grounding each Observed Pattern in the corresponding source construct. The enclosing function provides the local control- and data-flow context. When a precondition depends on information beyond the function, PerfR retrieves relevant type, global, and function definitions, together with project-local call sites, through the project-wide symbol index as dependency context . The source region ℓ i \ell_{i} , matched cards, and collected context together form a region-specific optimization prompt. Figure 2 illustrates this construction for the zrsh loop, where the definitions of zahl and zahl_char_t provide dependency context for (*a).chars . Based on the region-specific prompt, the agent first evaluates the rewrite preconditions of each matched card against the supplied program context. Cards with unmet or unresolved preconditions are excluded; if no card remains, PerfR skips the region. Otherwise, the agent jointly considers the Optimization Directions of the applicable cards and synthesizes a single candidate rewrite for ℓ i \ell_{i} . When multiple directions affect overlapping code, they are coordinated within the same rewrite rather than applied independently.

paragraphs.en: Applying a candidate rewrite may cause either (i) behavioral deviation or (ii) runtime regression despite preserving behavior. PerfR therefore validates every candidate for both functionality and performance before acceptance. The refined Rust project serves as the prepared baseline and initializes the current accepted version. A candidate is applied to this version and becomes the new accepted version only if it passes both validations; otherwise, the previous version is restored.

paragraphs.en: Functional Validation. Before rewriting begins, PerfR replays the functional workloads from § V-A on the prepared baseline to verify their recorded reference digests. For each candidate, PerfR rebuilds the project and re-executes the same operation–input pairs with the same harnesses. A candidate passes functional validation only if the build succeeds, all executions complete normally, and every output digest matches its reference. Otherwise, PerfR invokes a feedback-driven repair loop following prior LLM-based program repair [ 52 , 13 ] . The available diagnostics and source locations, together with the attempted rewrite and relevant program context, are returned to the agent for revision. The revised candidate is rebuilt and revalidated until it passes or the repair budget is exhausted, after which the candidate is discarded.
paragraphs.zh: 功能验证。 在开始重写之前，PerfR 会在准备好的基线上重放 § V-A 中的功能工作负载，以验证其记录的参考摘要。 对于每个候选项，PerfR 会重新构建项目，并使用相同的测试工具重新执行相同的操作–输入对。 只有当构建成功、所有执行正常完成且每个输出摘要都与参考摘要匹配时，候选项才能通过功能验证。 否则，PerfR 会遵循先前基于 LLM 的程序修复方法 [ 52 , 13 ] 启动反馈驱动的修复循环。 可用的诊断信息和源代码位置，连同已尝试的重写内容以及相关的程序上下文，会被返回给智能体以进行修订。 修订后的候选项会被重新构建并重新验证，直到通过验证或修复预算耗尽为止，此后该候选项将被丢弃。

paragraphs.en: Performance Validation. An Optimization Direction does not guarantee an end-to-end speedup, as semantics-preserving rewrites may alter compiler optimizations and machine-code layout [ 53 , 54 ] . PerfR therefore evaluates each functionally valid candidate using two complementary performance gates. Measurements use paired runs of the candidate and the corresponding reference version on each performance workload, with execution order alternated across pairs. Confidence intervals are computed for per-operation and aggregate runtime changes, and inconclusive cases receive additional measurements within a predefined budget. The incremental gate compares the candidate against the current accepted version on workloads associated with the rewritten hot function, ensuring that the new rewrite does not introduce a statistically supported regression beyond the predefined tolerance. Its aggregate decision weights operations by the hot function’s execution contribution. The cumulative gate compares the candidate against the prepared baseline across all measurable performance workloads, ensuring that successive accepted rewrites continue to provide a project-wide net gain. It uses an equal-weight aggregate and additionally guards against severe operation-level regressions that could be hidden by the aggregate result. Candidates with unresolved decisions or measurement failures at budget exhaustion are rejected.

paragraphs.en: Implementation. PerfR combines AST-based Rust source analysis with a project-wide symbol index, optimized LLVM IR and optimization-remark analysis, and perf -based cycle profiling. All LLM-based components use GPT-5.4 [ 55 ] . Workload synthesis targets 70% public-function coverage, with at most three coverage-refinement rounds and five harness-repair attempts. Hotspot localization retains project-owned functions with project-level hotness h ⁡ ( f ) h(f) of at least 3%. Internal performance validation uses two-sided 95% confidence intervals with adaptive sampling at 10, 20, and 40 measurement pairs. The per-operation and aggregate regression tolerances are 1.0% and 0.3%, respectively, and accepted rewrites must provide at least 0.1% project-wide net gain.

paragraphs.en: Evaluation Settings. We use the Evaluation Dataset workloads, build configuration, execution environment, measurement protocol, and runtime-overhead metric defined in § III-A and § III-B . To control code-placement effects in per-operation comparisons, we additionally compile all variants, including C, with 64-byte function alignment. We run Codex using CLI v0.153.4 with the same GPT-5.4 model as PerfR and reasoning effort set to high . We evaluate all variants on the same workloads and report timings only for operation–input pairs whose outputs are identical to those of C.

paragraphs.en: Table V compares Refined , PerfR R , and PerfR to assess the contribution of rule guidance. Translation Refinement and unguided optimization can both improve runtime on individual operations, but their gains are limited compared with PerfR . paragraphs.en: To understand how rule guidance contributes to these gains, we further examine the rewrites retained after validation. PerfR yields 62 accepted rewrites, compared with 28 for PerfR R . The two variants also differ in the types of transformations they produce. Among the 28 rewrites accepted under PerfR R , 16 are local cleanups; none recovers additional slice views or removes residual bounds checks, leaving the raw-pointer accesses remaining after refinement unchanged. In contrast, 46 of the 62 rewrites accepted by PerfR involve Memory Property Recovery , making access relationships and invariants explicit to LLVM. These results indicate that rule guidance changes not only the number but also the nature of accepted rewrites, directing optimization toward the performance mechanisms identified in our empirical study.

paragraphs.en: Beyond runtime performance, we examine the safety-related effects of PerfR across the 12 projects, considering both the caller-visible unsafe interface and raw-pointer use within rewritten functions. In RawRust , 99.8 % 99.8\% of functions are declared unsafe fn ; Codex leaves this proportion unchanged, whereas PerfR reduces it to 60.5 % 60.5\% , increasing the proportion of functions callable from safe Rust from 0.2 % 0.2\% to 39.5 % 39.5\% . This narrower interface is established during Translation Refinement and preserved by subsequent optimization. Relative to Refined , the optimized functions further reduce pointer-arithmetic operations by 18 % 18\% and raw-pointer dereferences by 10 % 10\% through transformations such as slice-based traversal and iterator-based access. Overall, PerfR improves performance while narrowing the caller-visible unsafe interface and further reducing reliance on raw-pointer memory operations.

paragraphs.en: One threat concerns the sensitivity of runtime measurements to system noise. We mitigate this threat by using five warm-up rounds and 30 paired measurements for each workload, alternating the C–Rust execution order, and compiling all compared variants with consistent function alignment. Another threat concerns the representativeness of performance evaluation within each project. Rather than using a single whole-project runtime or isolated API calls, we evaluate semantically complete end-to-end operations that exercise distinct implementation paths and use multiple operations when a project contains different performance-relevant functionalities. A third threat concerns potential bias in the optimization rules toward the projects from which they are derived. We mitigate this threat by deriving the rules exclusively from the eight Study-Dataset projects and reserving twelve disjoint projects for evaluation.
paragraphs.zh: 一项威胁涉及运行时测量对系统噪声的敏感性。 我们通过以下方式缓解这一威胁：为每个工作负载使用五轮预热和30次成对测量，交替C–Rust的执行顺序，并以一致的函数对齐方式编译所有被比较的变体。 另一项威胁涉及每个项目内性能评估的代表性。 我们没有使用单一的全项目运行时间或孤立的API调用，而是评估语义完整的端到端操作，这些操作会执行不同的实现路径；当项目包含不同的与性能相关的功能时，我们使用多个操作。 第三项威胁涉及优化规则对其所来源的项目可能存在的偏差。 我们通过仅从八个Study-Dataset项目推导规则，并保留十二个不相交的项目用于评估，来缓解这一威胁。

paragraphs.en: Automated code translation spans both function- and project-level migration across multiple language pairs [ 57 , 58 , 59 , 60 , 61 , 62 , 63 , 64 ] . We focus on project-level C-to-Rust translation, where existing approaches broadly follow two routes. LLM-based translators aim to generate safer and more idiomatic Rust, increasingly leveraging program analysis and project-wide context to improve translation quality [ 65 , 21 , 12 , 13 ] . Preserving source behavior, however, remains challenging at project scale. Rule-based translators such as Corrode [ 66 ] and c2rust [ 8 ] instead apply deterministic transformations to C constructs, yielding reproducible translations intended to preserve source behavior. Such translations often retain C-oriented representations, including raw pointers and extensive unsafe code [ 10 ] . To improve C-to-Rust translation, prior work has explored program-analysis-based refinement [ 10 , 19 , 9 ] , LLM-guided rewriting [ 65 , 21 ] , and project-wide reasoning over dependencies and pointer semantics [ 12 , 13 ] . These efforts primarily target behavioral preservation, safety, and idiomaticity. In contrast, PerfR starts from mechanically translated Rust and focuses on recovering runtime performance lost during translation.

sents.en: To improve C-to-Rust translation, prior work has explored program-analysis-based refinement [ 10 , 19 , 9 ] , LLM-guided rewriting [ 65 , 21 ] , and project-wide reasoning over dependencies and pointer semantics [ 12 , 13 ] .
sents.zh: 为改进 C 到 Rust 的翻译，已有工作探索了基于程序分析的精化 [ 10 , 19 , 9 ] 、LLM 引导的重写 [ 65 , 21 ] ，以及基于依赖关系和指针语义的项目级全局推理 [ 12 , 13 ] 。

sents.en: In contrast, PerfR starts from mechanically translated Rust and focuses on recovering runtime performance lost during translation.
sents.zh: 相比之下，PerfR 从机械翻译得到的 Rust 代码出发，专注于恢复翻译过程中丢失的运行时性能。

paragraphs.en: Recent work has begun to investigate performance regressions introduced by C-to-Rust translation. Xia et al. compare randomly generated C programs with their c2rust translations and identify Relooper-induced code duplication as one source of runtime overhead [ 24 ] , while RUSTY targets this control-flow expansion through a specialized translation scheme [ 27 ] . However, they either rely on synthetic programs or address a specific translation-induced mechanism, leaving performance divergence and recurring code-level causes in real-world projects less well characterized. Beyond translation-specific performance studies, SemOpt derives reusable optimization strategies from historical commits [ 28 ] , and MoST extends such knowledge across multiple sources, languages, and scenarios [ 29 ] . While these approaches demonstrate the value of rule-guided optimization, their guidance is general-purpose rather than derived from performance differences introduced by code translation. Our work connects these two directions by analyzing paired C–Rust performance in real-world projects, distilling recurring code-level performance patterns and optimization directions into reusable rules, and applying them to guide post-translation performance recovery.
paragraphs.zh: 近期的工作已开始研究由 C 到 Rust 翻译引入的性能退化。 Xia 等人将随机生成的 C 程序与其 c2rust 翻译结果进行比较，并指出 Relooper 引起的代码重复是运行时开销的来源之一 [ 24 ] ，而 RUSTY 则通过一种专门的翻译方案来解决这种控制流膨胀问题 [ 27 ] 。 然而，这些工作要么依赖合成程序，要么只针对某种特定的翻译引入机制，使得真实项目中的性能差异及其反复出现的代码层面成因尚未得到充分刻画。 在翻译相关的性能研究之外，SemOpt 从历史提交中提炼可复用的优化策略 [ 28 ] ，MoST 则将这类知识扩展到多种来源、语言和场景 [ 29 ] 。 尽管这些方法展示了规则引导优化的价值，但它们的指导是通用性的，而非源自代码翻译引入的性能差异。 我们的工作将这两个方向联系起来：通过分析真实项目中的 C–Rust 配对性能，将反复出现的代码层面性能模式与优化方向提炼为可复用的规则，并将其应用于指导翻译后的性能恢复。

paragraphs.en: Across 20 real-world projects, we studied performance degradation in automated C-to-Rust translation and identified nine recurring performance issues and optimization directions through paired C–Rust analysis. We then developed PerfR , a rule-guided framework for locating and optimizing these issues. On twelve held-out projects, PerfR preserves C outputs on all 41 operations and improves runtime over c2rust on 40, demonstrating the value of empirically derived knowledge for cross-project performance recovery.
